f18c61e814.q: Why do companies learning to build software with AI still face high costs instead of free solutions?
f18c61e814.a: Even if building with AI, companies end up buying tokens instead of paying license fees, paying for consumption and addition. They still have to manage, maintain, and staff the system. Maintenance is not free and must be part of cost calculations. Additionally, SaaS providers offer best-in-class processes built into software from dozens or hundreds of clients, plus updated regulations and ongoing improvements that internal builders must replicate themselves.

0fe03e847c.q: What is day two AI debt and why does it matter for agentic systems?
0fe03e847c.a: Day two AI debt refers to ongoing maintenance problems that must be accounted for when deploying AI systems, including model deprecation and data line drift. These are essential considerations when engineering agentic systems, as they add significant complexity beyond the initial build phase.

7eb318c388.q: How can agentic AI improve claims processing containment rates in life insurance?
7eb318c388.a: A life insurer working with Capgemini increased their claim status self-service rate from 45% containment with legacy IVR systems to 80% with agentic chatbot solutions, while simultaneously increasing customer satisfaction from 46% to 70%. The AI systems handle FNRL intake and claim status inquiries, failing gracefully by calling for human help when encountering situations above thresholds or never seen before.

978976b159.q: How should claims adjusters' roles evolve with agentic AI implementation?
978976b159.a: One Capgemini client described the transformation as moving adjusters from firefighters to concierges. Technology takes burdensome reactive tasks off their plate—handling status calls, managing inquiries—and puts humans in a supervisory loop where they focus on thinking and decision-making rather than data entry or routine information lookups.
